drafted_from: tool:read-objects-in-an-s3-store row in tool-rows.json, do-work/read-objects.mjs and test/read-objects.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "List the files under site/ in my connected R2 store, then read site/index.html." It runs tool:read-objects-in-an-s3-store with your store connection, lists one page of objects and reads the one file.
no_lists_because: It names no list: it reads a bucket through your connected store and answers object names, sizes and bytes, writing and deleting nothing.
instructions: 1. Connect your S3-compatible store (Cloudflare R2 is one) so a service connection such as service_connection:cloudflare-r2 holds its key, endpoint and bucket; the key never appears in the request.

2. Say "List the files in my store" (add prefix or max_keys) or "Read the file <key>"; your AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:read-objects-in-an-s3-store and input {account_id, action, ...}.

3. Read the answer: a list gives objects [{key, size, last_modified}], truncated and next_token (pass it back as continuation_token for the next page); a get gives key, size, content_type and base64 (objects up to 10 MB).
4. If the store refuses the key (401 or 403) connect the store again with a current key; a missing key or bucket answers what was not found.

worked_examples.title: Read one page of a site's files, then one file
worked_examples.ask: List the files under site/ in my R2 store and read index.html.
worked_examples.given:
From tools/read-objects-in-an-s3-store/test/read-objects.test.mjs: the connected store has the made-up endpoint https://example-account.r2.example.test and bucket example-bucket, and the object index.html holds the 11 bytes

Hi

with content type text/html. The tool sends one signed GET to that endpoint only.
worked_examples.hands_back: {key: "index.html", size: 11, content_type: "text/html", base64: "PGgxPkhpPC9oMT4="}. The listing call with input {account_id, action: "list", prefix: "site/"} sends one GET to /example-bucket?list-type=2&max-keys=100&prefix=site/ and, when the bucket holds only index.html of 5 bytes, answers {objects: [{key: "index.html", size: 5, last_modified: "2026-11-01T00:00:00.000Z"}], truncated: false, next_token: null}. A 403 from the store answers "The store refused the held key (403). Connect the store again with a current key."
